question.text: On top of all of their other controversies, the Tokyo Olympics experienced one of the most intense heat waves ever to hit the Summer Olympics. As a result, some events were moved to this city on Hokkaido, which also hosted the 1972 Winter Olympics.

swap.leadin: This period succeeded the Tokugawa Shogunate.
swap.text: Name this period of rapid industrialization and modernization under a namesake emperor from 1869 to 1912 in Japan. The goals of the Emperor, restored to full power, were outlined in the Charter Oath.
swap.clue: In addition to the creation of the Charter Oath, this event also saw the passage of a constitution modeled on Prussia's.

question.text: The last American carrier lost in the war, the USSBismarck Sea, was lost at the battle to capturethisJapanese island. The fighting was immortalized by photographer Joe Rosenthal on Mount Suribachi.
question.clue: Much later in the war, American forces placed a flag on Mount Suribachi during a battle on this small Japanese island.

swap.text: Maejima Hisoka, the founder of the Japanese postal service, successfully petitioned the Meiji oligarchy that the official capital of Japan be moved from Kyoto to this city, then called Edo.
swap.clue: The Place That Was Promised and Underground chronicled a terrorist attack in this city carried out by a group now called Aleph.

question.leadin: This battle saw the use of Portuguese arquebuses, and one side of this battle consisted of forces loyal to Toyotomi Hideyori.
question.text: Name this battle that saw the forces of Ishida Mitsunari and Mori Terumoto defeated by those of Tokugawa Ieyasu, thereby establishing his namesake shogunate.
question.clue: The capture of Konosu and Gifu Castles preceded this battle, whose decisive moment saw a staged round of arquebus fire signal a force of turncoats to attack the army of their initial ally Otani instead.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the restoration of the Meiji ["may-jee's"] Emperor's power.
swap.text: This declaration was issued by the Meiji Emperor after he took the throne. "Evil customs of the past" were done away with after this document was issued, as it paved the way for the westernization of Japan.
swap.answerHtml: Charter Oath [or Gokajo no Goseimon; or the Oath in Five Articles]
swap.clue: This document was created when Emperor Meiji took power in 1868. It laid out Meiji's goals for Westernization, and can be considered the first constitution of modern-day Japan.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the history of Japan.
question.text: This period in Japanese history is named after its capital, present-day Kyoto. Preceded by the Nara period and followed by the Kamakura shogunate, it ended in the Genpei War.
question.clue: The Fujiwara clan held de facto power during this period, which was ended by the Genpei ] War and began when Emperor Kanmu moved the capital to Kyoto.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Hojo clan.
swap.text: The Hojo were the effective rulers during this shogunate named for a city that's today famous for a large Buddha statue. This shogunate took power after the Heian period.
swap.clue: Its puppet rulers attempted to revolt with the Jokyu war, but were crushed and remained silent for another century.

question.leadin: During this era, a period of economic expansion and the flourishing of the arts took place in its Genroku Period.
question.text: Identify this government that was ended by an era of rapid industrialization called the Meiji restoration. Ieyasu was its first leader.
question.answerHtml: Tokugawa Shogunate [or Tokugawa Period; or Edo Period; or Tokugawa Bafuku; or Edo Bafuku]
question.clue: Supporters of this dynasty lost at the Battle of Hakodate after starting the Ezo Republic during the Boshin War.

swap.text: The Japanese public was mostly unaware that they were a few months away from starving to death when Portsmouth was signed, instead focusing on its inadequate reflection of the Battle of Mukden and this crushing naval victory for Togo Heihachiro.
swap.clue: At the end of this battle, Admiral Nebogatov surrendered rather than doom his 2,000-plus sailors; regardless, his fleet had lost six battleships and twenty-eight other ships in a single day after eight months of sailing from the Baltic Sea.

question.text: The Tokugawa shogunate was ended and Emperor Mutsuhito oversaw an extensive modernization program during this nineteenth-century era.
question.clue: Established in the wake of the Boshin War by the five-article Charter Oath, it abolished the feudal han system and saw a massive industrialization campaign that led to military triumphs over China and Russia.

swap.text: The Meiji emperor put down this 1877 rebellion, led by Saigo Takamori, who lamented the loss of power of his fellow Samurais. It fought its last battle at Shiroyama.
swap.clue: Many leaders of this movement were on the losing side of the Seikanron Debate, in which they had unsuccessfully advocated a war, and thereafter they had resigned and returned to their home prefecture.

question.text: In correspondence with Emperor Yang of Sui, this prince encouraged him to call Japan by Nihon. Through the Seventeen-Article Constitution, he promoted Buddhism as Japan's state religion.

swap.text: The importance placed on the renunciation of imperial divinity is noted in this 1999 book by John W. Dover that explores the occupation and democratization of Japan after World War II.

question.leadin: A popular legend about a member of this clan states that he survived an assassination attempt, fled to Mongolia, and became Genghis Khan, which was popularized during the interwar period to justify invading China.
question.text: Name this samurai clan that included the assassinated Yoshitsune, who defeated the monk Benkei on a bridge. This clan allied with the Hojo to defeat the Taira.
question.clue: They were defeated by their main rivals in the Heiji Rebellion, after which many of them were mercifully sent into exile including Noriyori, the younger brother of the main members.

swap.leadin: Ka'en jars, with tops that resemble flames, were principally produced during the middle of this period.
swap.text: Name this period, which gets its name from using rope to make marks on pottery. The Yayoi culture succeeded this period.
swap.clue: This period's namesake hunter-gatherers were supplanted by the agricultural Yayoi ] people.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Jomon and Epi-Jomon cultures and peoples.
question.text: The term "Zoku" or "Epi-" Jomon refers to the persistence of Jomon patterns in northern Japan past when this culture superseded it further south. Wet rice agriculture became dominant in this culture's namesake period.

swap.leadin: Identify these leaders of 20th century Japan.
swap.text: This man served as Emperor of Japan from 1912 to 1926. His reign is considered a golden age of Japanese democracy.
swap.clue: This ruler, who ceded regency power to his son due to psychological problems. His country sent a list of twenty-one demands to a neighbor.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Empress Saimi, who reigned from 642 to 645 AD if we are to believe the historical record.
question.text: That data appears in this chronicle, which like the Kojiki, is semi-mythical. The first petrochemical oil spill in ancient literature appears in this text's chronicle of Emperor Tenji.
question.clue: This set of chronicles, the most comprehensive text available for scholarship on Ancient Japan. It was completed under the supervision of Prince Toneri and presented to Empress Gensho in the year 720.

swap.text: During the Kenmu Restoration, Nitta Yoshisada helped win a big victory over this group at Kamakura. A member of this clan traditionally held the position of shikken, and later they were defeated by Hideyoshi at the Siege of Odawara.
swap.clue: Many prominent members of this line committed seppuku after invasion of the general Nitta Yoshisada.
